findings.title: The new SDF_LZ4 branch takes over the UE_IO branch's `return`, so IoStore jobs now fall through.
findings.body:
The new `if ... == SDF_LZ4:` (4 spaces) and its call are inserted between `ue_io_shaders(...)` and that branch's `return rel, uniq_keys(found), ...`, which is still indented 8 spaces. After the patch, that `return` belongs to the SDF_LZ4 branch. A UE_IO job (IoStore export bundles from `ue_legacy_jobs`) now runs `ue_io_shaders`, skips the SDF_LZ4 check, and continues into the FB_CAS check and whatever loose scanning follows. It no longer returns its export-bundle shaders right away, so the container gets scanned again or misread, and its results change. This looks like a bad resolution of the rebase conflict next to the IoStore reader. The fix is to give the UE_IO branch its own `return` again and give the SDF_LZ4 branch its own, like this:
```
        ue_io_shaders(path, rel, args[2][1], found)
        return rel, uniq_keys(found), var_pairs(found), trees
    if len(args) > 2 and args[2][0] == SDF_LZ4:
        sdf_list_shaders(path, rel, args[2][1], found)
        return rel, uniq_keys(found), var_pairs(found), trees
```

held.title: Each SDF slice is now both a `big` job and a loose `files` job under the same `rel`.
held.body: `sdf_list_jobs` returns an empty exclusion set, so every slice that has a part-list job also stays in `files` and is scanned loosely too. Every other reader here takes its paths out of `files`. Both jobs return the same `rel`. If the results are merged by `rel` (for example in a dict keyed by file), the loose scan's empty result for a version 23 slice can overwrite the shaders found through the part list, or the other way round. The split then finds nothing for Starlink again. I could not see how `main` merges the results. Please check it, or merge the results for the same `rel` explicitly.
